Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  AI in Cyber Security [IT_4004]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Analyze the differences in performance between supervised and unsupervised learning                     (5)  
  approaches when applied to anomaly detection in cybersecurity. Which approach is more effective  
  A)           under zero-day attack conditions, and why?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Differentiate between threats, vulnerabilities, and attacks in the context of cybersecurity. Provide (5)  
  a suitable example for each and explain how they are interrelated in a real-world cyber incident.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"

  A)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"

B)         Critically analyze the case study of ransomware behaviour classification using machine                (5)  
  learning. Discuss how real-time monitoring and feature engineering contribute to early detection.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)              Suppose a cybersecurity analyst is tasked with identifying ransomware attacks from system log         (5)  
  data. Explain how the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classification algorithm can be applied to detect  
  A)         and classify ransomware activities. Describe the steps involved in feature extraction, distance  
  computation, model training, and decision-making based on the nearest neighbors.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Describe how an Autoencoder can be trained for network anomaly detection. Explain how                 (5)  
  reconstruction error is used to distinguish between normal and malicious network traffic.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)              Discuss how RNNs and LSTMs capture sequential patterns in network traffic to detect brute-force       (5)  
  or port-scan attacks.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Deep Learning models can automatically extract latent patterns from high-dimensional network          (5)  
  traffic data. Analyze how Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) can be used to detect packet  
  anomalies by treating packet headers as structured data or visual representations.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)              Define an adversarial attack in the context of machine learning. Using an example, explain how a (5)  
  small perturbation or noise added to an input (e.g., an image) can mislead a deep neural network  
  A)         classifier.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Illustrate with a labelled diagram the taxonomy of adversarial attacks based on attacker              (5)  
  knowledge (White-box, Black-box, and Gray-box). Explain how the attacker's access to the  
  model affects the type of attack used  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
